title: Baked Clams Oreganata
subtitle: Clams topped with herbed breadcrumbs and baked until golden
excerpt: Fresh clams halved on the shell, covered in a garlicky dried breadcrumb mix and baked hot. A classic Italian-American starter that takes minutes to put together.
sourceNotes: Italian-American seafood staple from the New York and New Jersey coastline. Synthesised from multiple restaurant and home cook sources.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Fill the shells up to 2 hours ahead and refrigerate. Bake just before serving.

content.text: Baked clams oreganata is a quick Italian-American classic. The breadcrumb topping should be golden and just crisp on top while the clam stays juicy underneath. Use the freshest clams you can find.

items.prepNote: scrubbed clean, opened and on the half shell

content.text: Heat the oven to 220C. Line a baking tray with foil and scatter a little salt on it to help steady the shells.
Mix the breadcrumbs, parmesan, garlic, parsley, oregano, lemon zest, chilli flakes, salt and pepper in a bowl.
Add 3 tablespoons of the olive oil to the crumb mix. Toss until the crumbs look damp but not wet.
Arrange the clams on the half shell on the tray. Spoon a generous pile of crumbs onto each one.
Drizzle the remaining olive oil over the top of each clam.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes until the crumbs are golden and the clam edges have curled slightly.
Squeeze lemon juice over them and serve straight from the tray.

items.symptom: The crumbs are pale and soft.
items.cause: The oven was not hot enough, or there was too much oil in the mix.
items.fix: Make sure the oven is fully up to temperature before the tray goes in. Use just enough oil to moisten the crumbs.

items.symptom: The clams taste tough and rubbery.
items.fix: Check them at 8 minutes. The clam only needs enough heat to warm through. Pull them out as soon as the crumbs colour.

items.symptom: The shells tip over and lose juice.
items.cause: The tray surface is too smooth.
items.fix: Scrunch a sheet of foil into a rough bed on the tray. Press each shell gently to settle it before filling.
